cases.title: A many join turns one upstream row into one row per matching record, each carrying its own source records
A many join drops an upstream row that matches nothing rather than projecting it half empty
Four members are in the selected band, which is the row count a join has to be measured against
A one join contributes at most one record per upstream row and drops the row that matches nothing
The join field 'id' means the record's own id on whichever side declares it, so a junction needs no copy of it
A joined record the caller may not read is dropped exactly as an absent one is, disclosing nothing
The same record set projects the withheld row once read policy allows it, so the omission was policy and not absence
A many join is refused when the caller may not search the joined object, because the join enumerates it
A one join is refused on the same grounds, because the predicate enumerates the joined object either way
A source declaring no join still follows a loaded record's lookup field and reads one record by id
An undeclared lookup source still projects for a caller who may not search that object, because it reads one known id
LOOKUP ... TARGET_FIELD resolves an implicit read-model join by the named field, not by the target record's own id
A TARGET_FIELD lookup with no matching target record drops the row rather than erroring
Matching a TARGET_FIELD lookup by field value is a search, so it is refused without the search action on the target object
